decision.reason: It is the lowest-cost observable fail-closed repair: two FSM bits and two required ports, with no epoch comparator, wider identity, payload state, or normal pipeline stage. A stale/high/stuck acknowledgement cannot release service because recovery requires a new sampled low/high/low sequence.
decision.rejected_external_epoch_seed: A correct scheme must widen request/response identity and own a persistent unique seed. Finite-width epochs eventually wrap, and seed uniqueness remains an external contract. It costs more state, wires, and comparison logic than flushing the single outstanding response.
decision.rejected_atomic_macro_reset: It costs zero hardware but is not observable by the bridge. If the macro wrapper fails to erase an old response, the original same-token silent corruption remains possible, so this is an integration assumption rather than a fail-closed repair.

proposed_cost_and_performance.maximum_recovery_cycles: unbounded_until_wrapper_acknowledges; this is intentional fail-closed safety

positive_findings: The selected low/high/low handshake rejects both the exact M137 reset-token replay and a stale acknowledgement that is already high when reset releases.

The proposal changes only recovery control. It preserves M137's one-outstanding, one-skid, 16-bit token and one-cycle fallthrough normal path, so it requires no architectural II or delivery-latency penalty.
The specification distinguishes safe pre-completion drain traffic from an unsafe return concurrent with or after claimed flush completion.
The directed matrix attacks reset at pending, fallthrough, skid-full, pop-plus-new and recovery-handshake phases, then reruns the 128-request and 65,538-request M137 regressions.

The trust boundary is explicit: flush acknowledgement certifies destruction of all partial-bank, aggregate-response, and token-echo state; a wrapper that lies after acknowledgement is not claimed to be detectable by token-only M139.
Claim flags remain false for RTL, VCS, Formality, DC, physical speedup, system speedup and headline evidence.

findings.title: The repair is a specification, so the production M137 silent reset alias remains open
findings.observation: No M139 RTL, wrapper handshake, SVA, or VCS execution is present in this review package. The existing production M137 interface still lacks epoch ownership.
findings.impact: The old pre-reset token-0000 payload can still be accepted as a post-reset token-0000 response in production. The 93/100 score assesses implementation readiness of the specification, not defect closure.
findings.required_fix: Implement the exact two-bit four-phase FSM and two required ports, then pass all twenty directed rows plus the frozen M137 and natural-wrap regressions before marking the M137 P1 closed.

findings.title: Flush acknowledgement remains a trusted macro-wrapper guarantee
findings.observation: M139 can validate handshake ordering and reject responses before release, but it cannot distinguish a wrapper that acknowledges completion and later replays an old payload with the exact token of a new pending request.
findings.impact: The repair is fail closed for handshake and timing violations visible at the interface, not Byzantine-macro tolerant.
findings.minimal_fix: Assert inside the 16-bank wrapper that acknowledgement covers every partial return, aggregate-valid, token, and response-pipeline state, and that none can reappear after acknowledgement. Use an echoed epoch only if that wrapper proof cannot be established.

findings.title: Recovery is safe but not bounded for liveness
findings.observation: A stuck-high or stuck-low acknowledgement leaves the bridge quarantined indefinitely. The minimum clean handshake takes three sampled transition edges before RUN, but no maximum exists.
findings.impact: Safety is preserved, while system availability depends on the wrapper's bounded flush latency.
findings.minimal_fix: Specify and verify a wrapper latency bound. If diagnosability is required, add a watchdog that only raises sticky protocol_error and never auto-releases recovery.

findings.title: No-cycle-impact does not yet imply no frequency or area impact
findings.observation: The proposal adds no normal pipeline stage and keeps II1/one-cycle delivery architecturally, but the RUN decode and quarantine gates have not been synthesized or timed.
findings.impact: It is unsafe to call the repair zero-cost, frequency-neutral, or PPA-neutral before exact-SHA implementation evidence.
findings.minimal_fix: After VCS, run Formality and matched M137/M139 logic-only DC with identical 3 ns constraints, then integrate the real wrapper and macro-aware timing.

implementation_gates: Exact two-bit WAIT_LOW/WAIT_HIGH/WAIT_DROP/RUN FSM and two required ports only; no silent relaxation to a one-edge acknowledgement.
All service and token advancement blocked outside RUN and under sticky fault.
Exact M137 silent token-0000 replay demonstrably drains the old payload and delivers only the new payload.
All twenty attack-matrix rows executed with named cover or explicit trust-boundary classification.
M137 128-request/2048-word regression and 65,538-request natural token-wrap regression pass after recovery.
Exact-SHA VCS/SVA receipt before defect closure; Formality and DC before timing/area claims.
Wrapper-local assertions prove flush covers all sixteen banks and aggregate response state before macro-inclusive use.
claim_boundary: M139 r1 is a minimal synthesizable protocol proposal and frozen verification plan. It does not close the production M137 P1, and it admits no implemented functionality, commercial simulation, equivalence, timing, area, power, physical speedup, system speedup, DATE headline, or best-paper claim.
